title: What’s the best toothpaste to prevent tooth deterioration caused by suboxone?
body:
Been on suboxone for 6 years, my teeth have been consistently deteriorating ever since. I’ve done everything to try to slow it(except get off suboxone, I’m working on it), I brush 3 times a day, floss 2-3 times a day, and use fluoride mouthwash 3 times a day. 

The reason suboxone does this is because it’s so acidic, similarly to soda or candy, so use mouthwash after you take your dose, don’t brush your teeth though, your teeth will be more vulnerable after you dose. But has anybody found the most effective toothpaste? Because so far, having such good oral hygiene hasn’t helped much

Edit- I forgot, I also started using a waterpik twice a day, that should make a big difference, as the deterioration isn’t between my teeth or anything like that, it’s strictly only on the gum line
span_if_claim:
You are brushing too much. Just twice a day is sufficient. 
Brushing is what causes enamel erosion typically(combined with acidic foods and dry mouth). 
Get an electric toothbrush and just hold it over your teeth without brushing. 
Brush before subs and swish with water after usage. 
You’ll want a toothpaste that isn’t abrasive, so nothing with whitening.
Also drink tons of water.
comment: You are brushing too much. Just twice a day is sufficient. Brushing is what causes enamel erosion typically(combined with acidic foods and dry mouth). Get an electric toothbrush and just hold it over your teeth without brushing. Brush before subs and swish with water after usage. You’ll want a toothpaste that isn’t abrasive, so nothing with whitening. There’s a list that shows the abrasive ness of toothpastes online if you search for it. I think you want to avoid sensodyne, some of the arm and hammer are good, some of the crest too. I think Colgate usually has more abrasive ness to it, but again it’s not brand dependent, it just depends on the type. Also drink tons of water.

title: Some days I feel a strong "buzz" after taking my sub, and some days I barely notice any change at all. How do I get the most out of these strips?
body:
I've been on subs since January. It was great at first but, naturally, I've built quite a tolerance. I'm on 12mg a day.

As I said in the title, there's a big discrepancy day to day when taking taking my strips. Some days I get a strong buzz, which I appreciate because I take my subs in the afternoon when I have to get kids on the bus, run errands, and so on. This also gives me a break from my chronic pain. But some days when I take my strip, I feel almost no change at all.

I know that if you eat or drink while dissolving a strip it will wash away. Or it may dissolve too quickly and be swallowed. I've found that letting the strip dissolve slowly on the inside of my cheek tends to be the best way, sometimes it dissolves too quickly under my tongue, but even my cheek can be inconsistent.

Does anyone have any tips?

title: Suboxone emotional side effects?
body:
I've noticed that it is extremely hard for me to cry while on long term use of suboxone. I went to a funeral for a loved one and I cldnt cry like everybody else and I actually had to fake cry. It felt horrible. I truly was sad too but I just cldnt cry. When my dad went to the hospital for a heart attack I  cldnt cry when i saw him during the visit in the hospital. He is ok and fully recovered thanks to a change in lifestyle as well as his new plant based diet that literally reversed the clogging of his arteries and heart. 

Do you guys experience alot of ups and downs throughout the day and mood swings? 

Constipation? How to mitigate the symptoms?

I just got out of rehab a month ago and already started taking suboxone again because the depression was too great and the lack of motivation too. I'm still working out and exercising because that helps me feel good mentally and better about myself self consciously.

 Is it worth it to stay on it if I feel I need to?

There are many pros and cons. I'm much more productive now and I visit my family more instead of being in my room all day.  But....

Will I now have trouble getting a job because I'm on suboxone?  (Drug tests)

Anyways I wld really appreciate all of the advise and tips my fellow bropioids can give me. I love you all thankyou.
span_if_claim: Get things in place and stable in your life, get time under your belt sober and the mental/life tools in your toolbox before jumping off.
comment:
My thoughts are if you think you need it to stay sober then stay on it.  But I would still have the goal of getting off of it eventually, but don't rush it.  Get things in place and stable in your life, get time under your belt sober and the mental/life tools in your toolbox before jumping off.

Everyone is different but staying sober, healthy, and living a productive life is what is key in my view.  And if it takes Suboxone to do all that for now then so be it.  

It does make me a bit emotionally numb.  If I don't take it I'll have mood swings that come in huge waves and can be overwhelmed with sadness or even happiness.  But on it I'm kinda numb which is not where I want to be long-term.

title: 6 years on Suboxone and one year off: What I've Learned
body:
Man, this post is going to be brutally honest.

It was a rough road. I was on suboxone for 6 years: 8 mg for 2 years, 16mg for 4 years. On 9.29.20, I stopped cold turkey on Suboxone. I don’t recommend going cold turkey. Tapering is the safer choice. It was painful and I have not felt the same since emotionally (lack of emotions), but all other post withdrawal is gone. I want to give advice if you are beginning your withdrawal journey in the first 6 months off.

1. Do not take kratom. It will derail your progress of your natural dopamine production and you will not progress in your withdrawal timeline.
2. Low dose naltrexone (not vivitrol) is very good at healing dopamine receptors. Look into it.
3. Working out will help you more than I can say. I started with walks, and then kickboxing
4. Everyone's body is different and your journey may be easier or more difficult
5. The pain will end. You will be ok again.
6. If you are going to relapse or feel like it is a substantial possibility, do not get off.
7. Magnesium. Magnesium. Magnesium. And melatonin, vitamin D3, and robaxin. You will sleep :)
8. Find support. Friends, family. Let them know what you are feeling.
9. Eat foods with fiber and protein. The healthier you are, the shorter the withdrawal.
10. You are NOT alone.
span_if_claim: A beg to differ on not progressing your withdrawal timeline by using kratom. If used for a short amount of time, ideally less than 2 weeks, and doses limited, it should not prolong acute withdrawals.
comment:
A beg to differ on not progressing your withdrawal timeline by using kratom. If used for a short amount of time, ideally less than 2 weeks, and doses limited, it should not prolong acute withdrawals. Also, during acute withdrawals I don't think your natural dopamine production makes much, if any, progress anyways.
Though as you said, everyone is different.

Congrats on a year off subs, and thanks for sharing; a lot of good info.

title: Why no taper dose?
body:
I have been on suboxone for almost 10 years at this point. I have tried to stop a couple times but after suffering intense withdrawals lasting for 2-3 weeks without any end in sight, I always start up again because I had to be functioning for work and family. After failing to quit because of mentally and physical excruciating withdrawals I’ve become deterred to try again. 
It seems to me after doing deep research to get off this medication you need to be stable on .5-.25 a mg before jumping without suffering LONG withdrawal symptoms. Trying to cut a single 8 mg strip into 16-32 individual daily doses is a ridiculous task to make for someone. The fact that the lowest dose is 2 mg strips is almost proof the pharmaceutical companies have zero compassion for people that want to get off opiates. The goal isn’t ever to get your endorphin/opioid system back to normal but to make a lifelong patient of us. Not talking about those that need suboxone to stabilize there life, but those of us that have made permanent changes to our behavior. 
Well I am on day 6 of jumping from around 1mg, basically a speck of a 8mg strip. Today I wish I would of dropped down to a smaller dose before jumping last Wednesday but doesn’t seem realistic as smaller doses don’t exist and become impossible to accurately measure. Asking patient to cut up there strips in microscopic doses is such BS. 
When a normal .125-.2 mg form of buprenorphine becomes available and offered to patients that are ready to get back to their potential, then I will respect the MAT community rather than a group of big organizations that just wants to sink its hooks into us and our insurance.

title: A cautionary tale against kratom and why it's worse than being on Suboxone
body:
Let me preface this by saying that I used suboxone from 2006-2009 after a several year long addiction to oxycontin. I was clean for almost 7 years, then got hit by a car while crossing the street. I was back on prescription opiates for a few weeks, but not wanting to go back down that path again, I looked into pain relieving alternatives. That's when I found r/kratom. I then took kratom twice daily for almost two years and quickly became physically addicted to it.    

 

My experience getting off of suboxone was quite honestly a cake walk. Once I got to 2mg, I spent almost a year tapering down to zero and once I jumped completely, I felt 100% normal. As such, after dozens of failed attempts to taper down on kratom, I found myself back here considering using suboxone to treat my kratom addiction.  


 
 
That's when I started seeing an alarming trend: People that are at the end of their suboxone taper being recommended kratom. People that have been in treatment for a short time being told kratom is the better choice. People expressing interest in suboxone being told that they've got it all wrong, just get some kratom and you'll be happier for it. I personally got downvoted and all but called an absolute idiot for considering suboxone instead of kratom. I want to tell you guys why I think these recommendations are not only foolish, but downright counter-intuitive in relation to an addict that's trying to free themselves from their previous lifestyle.  
 
 

First, let's talk about the common side effects of kratom vs Suboxone:  

 

**Suboxone:**  
* Constipation  
* Diziness (at high doses)  
* Fatigue (at high doses)  
* Nausea (at high doses)  
* Physical withdrawal with missed doses  
* Urinary tract infections (in women)  

 

**Kratom:**  
*(Please feel free to search any of these terms in r/quittingkratom to see how common they truly are)*   
* Constipation  
* Hairloss    
* Fatigue   
* Physical withdrawal with missed doses (this typically starts between 5-8 hours after last dose once you're physically dependent)  
* Difficulty urinating      
* Incontinence  
* Nausea  
* Dizziness    
* Vomiting   
* "The wobbles" also known as pressure behind the eyes and inability to focus your eyes)  
* Lowered testosterone  
* Adrenal fatigue  
* Difficulty sleeping 

 

I will add that out of all of the side effects I have listed under kratom, I have experienced every single one (except lowered testosterone, I am a woman) personally almost every single day since I started. The worst ones are difficulty urinating (I can feel like my bladder is about to explode but be completely unable to pee for hours), hairloss (I lose clumps in the shower every single day and my eyebrows are falling out), and withdrawal between doses. I wake up every single morning with waterfalls of snot coming out of my nose, chills, achey joints, tears streaming down my face, and shortness of breath. That's just from sleeping through the night.  

 
   
But the biggest reason I think kratom is a terrible choice for the people in this sub is that it gets you high. Why haven't I quit despite all of the side effects listed above? Because I am an addict, and even after almost two years of being on kratom, I still get high twice a day, every single day. Suboxone can get you high for the first few days that you take it, but as long as you're using it correctly, it just keeps you stable and craving free. Don't throw your treatment down the toilet by trading suboxone for something that gets you high.

 

I hope that everyone will do their own research on what I have explained here. The reason you don't hear a lot of negative stuff about kratom is because r/kratom censors any negative comments or posts about the stuff because they're afraid it's going to be classified a schedule 1 substance. Some of them are also in the honeymoon phase of kratom abuse, where you've convinced yourself that you won't be like everyone else and you're experiencing few side effects. That will last a month, maybe two if you're lucky.  

 

So please be careful and speak up when people are recommending addictive substances to people that are just trying to get their lives back on track. Coming off of suboxone doesn't have to be hard as long as you're smart with your taper and don't try to jump off at too high of a dose or taper down too fast. I am more than happy to talk about how I was able to come off of suboxone painlessly, just let me know if that's something you would like to read about. This post is already long enough.  

 

**Edit:** A few of the responses claim that they still get "high" after months/ years of taking Suboxone. Not trying to be a dick here, but that isn't possible if you're taking the medication as prescribed. First of all, bupeprenorphine is only a partial agonist and has a high affinity but little intrinsic activity at the mu opioid receptors in the first place. Even with full agonist opioids, you would have to continually increase your dose to maintain the same effect on receptors over time. Kratom, on the other hand, has alkaloids that act as full agonists, similar to harder opiates like oxycodone, heroin, etc. Opiates will only continue getting you high over time if you increase the dose as your existing receptors become desensitized with repeated use.

For opiate addicts kratom should be viewed as another pain killer/opiate. Yes it is definitely not as harmful in multiple aspects as full blown opiates, but it has its downs as do most opiate like substances.

I've went through phases of sleep trouble. I've gotten head spins and dizzy (not quite like wobbles but similar balance issues). I've seen my friends who used suboxone for opiate addiction vomit and become insanely nauseas (I haven't personally had this issue as drugs rarely ever have induced these symptoms). Constipation is common as well for both kratom, suboxone, as well as any opiate like substance. I get urinary retention from suboxone despite my daily mg dose. This happens on kratom and any opiate for me as well. 

I agree with you that kratom isn't the "savior" plant for people on suboxone. Yet there are people I know and have seen feel less side effects on kratom vs suboxone maintenance. But the exception is NOT the rule. Drug addiction (with any substance) is a battle of self control. The more control you feel you have over the substance, the better off you physically and emotionally are (generally). Kratom must be dosed more often compared to suboxone due to the difference in half-life of the two substances. This makes suboxone far more desirable as a maintenance drug vs kratom. Just having to dose multiple times a day can cause old addictive tendencies and issues. Kratom can induce a "chase" to feel euphoria. So can suboxone, but it seems that kratom can provide a tiny bit more euphoria for a daily kratom users vs a daily suboxone user. Again, this could be a trigger and dangerous for someone who is in recovery.

The cons you have given for kratom seem not fully fleshed out. While your the suboxone list has *(at high doses)* caveat next to the side effects, you fail to do this for kratom. Wobbles are definitely a result of taking to much kratom. Likewise nausea, dizziness, vomiting, hair loss and fatigue are all normally associated with high doses and generally viewed as misuse of kratom as these effects are all undesirable. Also remember if you take to much kratom you don't get a nice peak of euphoria with your shitty side effects, usually you just feel like shit and regret taking too much. This is believe makes kratom extremely safe in comparison to popular and common opiates. Not even suboxone has this exact "natural built in" safety system. Reading your lists of cons, suboxone vs kratom seems slightly deceiving solely because you fail to distinguish high and low doses for kratom. 

Finally, the idea that kratom gets you "higher" than suboxone isn't as clear cut as you make it sound. Yes I agree that a single moderate to large dose of kratom will cause more euphoria vs buprenorphine in someone who IS USED TO BUPRENORPHINE. However, if you have ever seen someone take 1mg or even 0.5mg (or even less) with no tolerance for bupe, they will be far more high than someone who has no tolerance to kratom and takes a large dose of kratom. Both kratom and bupe have a similar ceiling effect when taken for maintence or pain daily. While kratom may induce more euphoria for a daily user (at times) vs a long term user of suboxone, it seems somewhat dishonest to suggest kratom gives maintenance users a dangerous opiate rush but suboxone never does. Even today, 10 years in, I get random days of semi intense euphoria on suboxone at 2mg maintence. I don't believe kratom is a better maintence drug for me personally, but I certainly don't believe it's worse for everyone or is inherently more dangerous to a user than bupe. I personally think that kratom should be legally available as a safer alternative to people who can't afford or access maintence drugs like suboxone or methadone. I do believe it's safety profile is largely similar to bupe and methadone as far as we know right now. There is no clear overdose deaths from kratom solely. Yet it certainly is not for everyone. 

Thanks for the post, I am always happy to read and engage in serious discussion on the pros and cons of opiate maintence and addiction.

title: Need to hear about your experience w subuxone
body: Im supposed to start the treatment with suboxone. im really desperate to get my life together for the first time, I need hope, cause I just cant live like this addict life anymore.. so i need to hear about your experience with it, i want to know if its worth trying..
span_if_claim: A lot of people can get through the detox once or twice and then make a couple days out there and then use again and you're screwed again.
comment:
If you've ever really gotten clean for like 3 weeks you realize how hard it is. A lot of people can get through the detox once or twice and then make a couple days out there and then use again and you're screwed again. But if you've made it to 3 weeks or 4 weeks you really understand how much of a slog a real cold turkey quit is. I personally couldn't do it. I was under performing at work, I was lazy, I was tired, I was no fun for my spouse, I was not interested in anything, big one here is that I wasn't sleeping, and every day was an absolute war that I could not sustain.

Suboxone for me lifted a lot of my negative symptoms like sadness and lethargy and got me able to go shopping and help at work more and be more like a regular human being... it's absolutely what I needed. I'm tapering off of it but I'm telling you using suboxone to break the bad habits and staying away from them for 6 months to a year is so much easier than trying at cold turkey, with having to fight all the cravings, and with life being as difficult as it's ever been. It's just a better way.

Edit:  I hate to put it like this but I'm going to... I find a lot of people who use suboxone are people who are trying to break their habit in the middle of sustaining their life either with their kids or their jobs and all the responsibilities that entails. A lot of the people who are going to tell you that you don't need suboxone are the actual rock bottomers who were able to quit with no job and nothing that they had to do for 6 months. That is totally possible and I understand where they're coming from too, 'don't get hooked on another substance if you've just got to quit that 1 too.' But a lot of us have to carry on with life, and so I always say if you're in a situation where you need to carry on with life and perform you should probably consider suboxone. If you've got family support and food and a roof over your head for 6 months and area to quit you might not need suboxone, you might be able to do it that way.

title: 5 days in cold Turkey from 12mg
body:
I took subs years ago and it really saved my life so there should be no shame in taking it and I am throwing no shade on suboxone. Years ago I took any pain pill for years( mainly norcos 5 to 8 1000s a day) because of my labor intensive job. Subs worked great. Forward years later smaller opiate addiction and big cocaine addiction. Went on subs and it was nothing like before. No motivation no sleep no appetite depressed. Still strong cravings. Just not myself for 6 months. Family and kids just watching me on the couch. Not sure why I’m sharing this but after a couple days off subs and a couple day coke binge I knew it was time to get clean. I can hardly explain how bad the wds are but I’m sure the worst of it is still to come. In a screwed up way I want to feel the pain as a reminder of why I want to be clean in the first place. Believe me i have regretted this decision multiple times already but I still feel it is what is best for me and my situation. (Though hours from now I may message differently) lol.  Everyone’s circumstances are different.  What works best for some may not for others. I’m praying for myself and for anyone else trying to break this evil cycle of addiction. Never stop trying to better yourself and don’t let any stigma or judging from others stop you from trying. 🙏🏼
Only you can find your own way.

When it gets the hardest is when you have to be a hard mother fucker, I never understood how much this concept strengthens you mentally. You’ll never question your strength again. I’m beyond proud of you and what you’re doing is beast mode monster shit. Embrace the pain and when it’s the worst look at yourself in the mirror and fucking scream, idk why but that helps lol. title: Buprenorphine for chronic pain
span_if_claim:
Buprenorphine plugs into every type of opioid receptor in the brain,
other opioids like oxycodone only act on specific opioid receptors. 
Dr.'s often overprescribe the strength of pain medicine as they want to make sure you're getting the relief you need. 
1 dose of bupe should provide approximately 12 hours of pain relief.  X 2/day for 24 hours.
comment:
Buprenorphine plugs into every type of opioid receptor in the brain, whereas other opioids like oxycodone only act on specific opioid receptors.  Point being is bupe provides a wider spectrum of pain relief. 

 I don't have chronic pain, that I know of, hard to tell when you've been on this stuff for years.  

But in my experience bupe is great at relieving every type of pain except dental nerve pain.  

If it relieves your fibromyalgia pain, then by all means take it. But try to take only as much as you need to knock out the pain.  Dr.'s often overprescribe the strength of pain medicine as they want to make sure you're getting the relief you need. 

I have a theory that suffering from chronic pain will only make your pain worse and wreak havoc on your body.  As pain is our body telling us something is wrong, but if you know something is wrong, and you keep hurting, then that pain is no longer serving a useful purpose to your body.  Plus most pain causes inflammation, and it's the inflammation part that wreaks havoc on your body.  Bupe is probably one of the best anti-inflammatory drugs out there because of it's long half life, and long duration of active pain relief. 

1 dose of bupe should provide approximately 12 hours of pain relief.  X 2/day for 24 hours. 

All I know is that while on Bupe, I experienced some interesting things.  Like not getting sick as often, getting over colds faster. Sports/work related muscle injuries that seem to resolve themselves in a day or 2. 
I got one of the worst sunburns of my life 4 years ago.  Took my suboxone dose, went to bed.  I woke up, and my sunburn was already peeling, my skin was no longer hot to the touch, and I wasnt in any pain like I was the night before.  I remember it used to take me 3 or 4 days to heal from a sunburn, not 1 night.

For better or worse though my personality is super chill on bupe.  Bupe definitely kills some of your passion.  But there's way too much of that in this world anyway.  Too many motherfuckers needing to get rich, sucking up a shit ton of resources while trying to live that yolo life.

I'm clean again now, but what a violent ride the whole ordeal was. Swear it aged me like 10-15 years.

body: I have been very worried about my doctors taper plan for me and I want to get some advice whether not I should be concerned. July 4th was my first dose and since then I have taken a total of about 22mgs. I'm noticing it becoming harder to stick to my 2 or 4 mg and may have to go up to eight since my first dose inducted me hard af unfortunately. Any suggestions? Am I tapering off too quick and am just being paranoid or is my concern legitimate? Thanks for any input. I can't tell if my doctor is just trying to make money or help. Even if he has good intentions he does not take the drug so he has some limited understanding of its potency. 2mg is alot...

You take that same dose each day once a day, for 3 to 5 days then stop.
You can't get addicted to methadone in such a short time. 
You will have greatly reduced or even eliminated all acute withdrawal symptoms.
this technique makes kicking pretty darn easy and painless. 
You can also kick this way with a few days of subs, but there's always the risk of precipitated withdrawal.

title: Need Help With Coming Off Kratom
body:
